papers.title: Extrinsic MANOVA for Oriented Projective Shapes
papers.abstract: For configurations of landmarks reconstructed from camera images, classical projective shape analysis identifies antipodal spherical representatives of projective coordinates, while oriented projective shape (OPS) retains their distinction. In 3D, a fixed oriented-projective coordinate representation of a OPS is point on product of 3D spheres. We develop nonparametric multisample inference for equality of population extrinsic means on this product. Quaternion multiplication helps create a global orthonormal tangent frame field, in which we obtain explicit extrinsic covariance blocks that preserve dependence between registered landmarks. A covariance-weighted MANOVA statistic has a chi-square null limit under nonfocality of distributions and positive-definite extrinsic covariance assumptions. An inverse-free discrepancy has a weighted chi-square limit when covariance matrices may be singular, and centered, groupwise nonparametric bootstrap procedures are justified asymptotically. We apply a fixed-observed-covariance nonparametric bootstrap version of the weighted statistic to 31 seven-landmark facial reconstructions from five subjects. Separate tests at the right inner brow and chin reject equality of the five OPS mean directions after Bonferroni adjustment. The analysis concerns a common mixed-sign frame domain and marginal landmarks; it does not establish pairwise subject differences or a joint six-dimensional facial test.

papers.title: Estimation and Inference for the Joint Autoregressive Quantile-Expected Shortfall Model
papers.abstract: Expected shortfall is defined as the truncated mean of a random variable that falls below a specified quantile level and is widely recognized as an important risk measure. Motivated by the empirical observation of clustering patterns in financial risks, we consider a joint autoregressive model for both conditional quantile and expected shortfall. Existing estimation methods for such models typically rely on minimizing a nonlinear and nonconvex joint loss function, which is challenging to solve. We introduce a two-step regression framework to estimate the model parameters with theoretical guarantees. We further develop a Portmanteau test for model diagnostics and prove its asymptotic validity for Type I error control. Our empirical results on stock market data indicate that the proposed models effectively capture the clustering patterns and leverage effects on the conditional expected shortfall.

papers.title: More Treatments More Problems: Designing the 2026 American Causal Inference Conference Data Challenge
papers.abstract: This paper documents the design of the 2026 American Causal Inference Conference (ACIC) Data Challenge, which uses a large set of simulations to evaluate the performance of a wide variety of causal inference estimators chosen and implemented by challenge participants. Unlike previous ACIC Data Challenges, which tended to mimic observational studies with a single binary treatment, the 2026 Data Challenge focused on randomized control trials with five arms (one control and four active treatments) to isolate key estimation challenges that arise when simultaneously estimating multiple treatment effects. We created 9,000 distinct synthetic populations corresponding to 18 distinct settings to explore variation in performance corresponding to patterns of treatment effect heterogeneity and response surface specifications. From each population, a sample of n = 1,000 was drawn for participants to estimate individual, subgroup, sample, and population-level treatment effects and identify the optimal treatment arm at each level. We describe several strategies used to generate the data to prevent Challenge participants from exploiting structural sim across datasets and ``gaming the system.'' By detailing these simulation design considerations and data generation choices, this paper provides a framework for conducting large-scale, unconfounded synthetic benchmark studies to rigorously evaluate multi-treatment causal inference procedures.
